package_info.why_malicious: The injected JavaScript code is designed to covertly collect sensitive payment card and personal information from checkout forms on restaurant ordering platforms and exfiltrate it to attacker-controlled domains. This constitutes credential theft and payment card fraud, as the data is stolen without user consent and sent to infrastructure controlled by cybercriminals.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when the checkout page is loaded and the user clicks the checkout button
execution_context.file_location: Injected into checkout page HTML/JavaScript (e.g., main.js, inline <script> tag)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the user clicks the checkout button, the code reads credit card number, expiration month and year, CVV2, and billing address from the form fields, concatenates them, and exfiltrates this data by dynamically creating a script tag with a source URL pointing to an attacker-controlled domain, resulting in covert theft of payment information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code surreptitiously collects sensitive payment data from form fields and transmits it to an external domain (authorizen.net) that is not associated with the legitimate payment processor, using a dynamically created script tag to evade detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate checkout scripts should only transmit payment data to trusted payment gateways via secure, documented POST requests, never by embedding sensitive data in a script tag's URL to an unknown domain.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or payment integrations may collect form data, but only transmit to trusted, documented endpoints using secure methods, and never send raw payment data to third-party domains.
key_indicators: Direct access to payment form fields (CC_number, cc_month, cc_year, cc_cvv2, CC_address)
Exfiltration of concatenated sensitive data to a suspicious domain (authorizen.net/ord.php)
Use of dynamically created script tag for data exfiltration
Event handler attached to checkout button (theme-btn)
No user notification or consent for data transmission

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when the user submits the checkout form
execution_context.file_location: Injected into MenuDrive platform checkout page as a separate script

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the user submits the checkout form, the code collects the cardholder's name, email, phone number, and payment card details from the DOM, then exfiltrates this data via an HTTP POST request to an attacker-controlled domain, resulting in unauthorized theft of personal and financial information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The script collects both personal and payment data from the checkout form and sends it to an external, non-legitimate endpoint (malicious-domain.com) using a fetch POST request, which is not part of the legitimate payment workflow.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scripts should only transmit sensitive data to the payment processor or backend server of the platform, never to unknown third-party domains, and should use secure, documented APIs.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate payment integrations may collect similar data, but only for processing payments with trusted providers and never transmit raw payment or PII data to untrusted domains.
key_indicators: Collection of both PII (name, email, phone) and payment data (card, exp, cvv)
Exfiltration of data to a non-standard, attacker-controlled domain (malicious-domain.com)
Use of fetch/XHR to send sensitive data externally
No user notification or consent for data transmission
Script not present in original platform codebase

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when the user interacts with a fake payment form overlay on the checkout page
execution_context.file_location: Injected into InTouchPOS platform checkout page as a fake form overlay
required_permissions: DOM access (create and read form fields)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the user interacts with the fake payment form overlay, the code creates a new form element on top of the legitimate checkout page, collects all entered payment and user data upon form submission, and exfiltrates this data to an attacker-controlled server, resulting in phishing and theft of sensitive information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The script creates a fake payment form overlay to phish user data, intercepts the form submission, and sends the collected information to an external domain controlled by the attacker.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate checkout pages should not overlay fake forms or intercept user data for external transmission; all payment data should be handled by the platform's secure, original forms and transmitted only to trusted endpoints.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; overlaying fake forms to intercept sensitive data is inherently malicious and has no legitimate use case.
key_indicators: Creation of new form elements that overlay or obscure the legitimate UI
Interception of form submission to capture user input
Exfiltration of sensitive data to an external domain
Absence of legitimate payment processing after form submission
Script not present in original platform codebase

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript is injected into the checkout page of restaurant ordering platforms, either inline or as separate scripts.
attack_chain.leads_to: The malicious code is present and ready to execute when users interact with the checkout page.

attack_chain.action: When a user enters payment details and interacts with the checkout form (e.g., clicking the checkout button or submitting the form), the malicious script collects sensitive data from the DOM or from a fake overlay form.
attack_chain.leads_to: Collection of payment card information and personally identifiable information (PII) from users.

attack_chain.action: The collected data is exfiltrated to attacker-controlled domains via HTTP requests (fetch/XHR) or dynamically created script tags.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives payment card and PII, enabling carding, identity theft, and fraud.

attack_chain.action: Stolen payment card data is aggregated and sold on dark web marketplaces or used directly for fraudulent transactions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Financial fraud and loss for victims, as well as reputational and regulatory impact for affected platforms.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript accessing payment form fields such as credit card number, CVV, expiration date, billing address, name, email, and phone on checkout pages
Exfiltration of form data to external domains via fetch, XMLHttpRequest, or dynamically created script tags
Creation of new form overlays or fake forms on top of legitimate checkout pages
Event handlers attached to checkout or payment buttons that trigger data exfiltration
file_indicators: Unexpected inline <script> tags or external script references on checkout pages
References to suspicious or lookalike domains (e.g., authorizen.net, malicious-domain.com) in script source URLs
Injected scripts or code blocks not present in the original platform codebase
Presence of new or modified JavaScript files (e.g., main.js) with unauthorized changes
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to domains such as authorizen.net/ord.php or malicious-domain.com/collect during checkout process
POST requests containing payment or PII data to unknown or untrusted domains
Unusual script loading activity from non-standard domains during checkout
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unexpected JavaScript accessing payment form fields and transmitting data to external domains. Scan for inline or injected scripts on checkout pages, especially those referencing suspicious or lookalike domains. Use web application firewalls (WAF) and content security policies (CSP) to block unauthorized script execution and outbound requests. Regularly audit subdomains and web assets for unauthorized code changes. Implement network monitoring to detect outbound requests to non-standard domains during checkout, and alert on POST requests containing payment or PII data to unknown endpoints.
